nodes.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$, the list of all letters of $\alpha$, each appearing exactly once, in some fixed but unspecified order.
nodes.title: List of all letters

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types and consider words over the disjoint union $\alpha \sqcup \beta$. For all words $u, v$ over $\alpha \sqcup \beta$, all $b \in \beta$ and $a \in \alpha$, all words $X$ over $\alpha$ and all words $Y$ over $\beta$, we have $u\,b\,a\,v \ne X\,Y$: a word over $\alpha$ followed by a word over $\beta$ never has a symbol of $\beta$ immediately followed by a symbol of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: No right symbol directly precedes a left symbol in a left-then-right word

nodes.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is a list of productions whose nonterminals $N_0, N_1, \dots$ are encoded as natural numbers and whose terminals are the letters $a \in \alpha$ and the two bits $\mathbf{t}$ (true) and $\mathbf{f}$ (false). Writing $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ for the unary code of an index $i$, the list consists of the productions $N_3 \to \varepsilon$,…
nodes.title: Domino-independent productions of the universality grammar

nodes.summary: The code of an index $i \in \mathbb{N}$ is the bit word $\mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ of length $i + 1$: the bit $\mathbf{t}$ (true) followed by $i$ copies of the bit $\mathbf{f}$ (false); with $|$ for true and $1$ for false, it is the word $|\,1^i$.
nodes.title: Unary code of an index

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $I = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers write $c(I) = c(i_1) \cdots c(i_n)$, where $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ is the unary code of $i$. If $I$ and $J$ are finite sequences of natural numbers with $c(I) = c(J)$, then $I = J$.
nodes.title: Concatenated index codes are uniquely decodable

nodes.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $J = (j_1, \dots, j_n)$ be a finite sequence of natural numbers with $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$. Write $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ for the unary code of $i$ and $c(J) = c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$. Then there are no bit words $Y$ and $Z$ with $c(J) = Y\,c(k)\,Z$.
nodes.title: Codes of indices below $k$ contain no code of $k$

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $I = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers, its code is the bit word $c(i_1)\,c(i_2) \cdots c(i_n)$, the concatenation of the unary codes $c(i) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^i$ of its entries; the empty sequence has the empty code.
nodes.title: Concatenated code of an index sequence

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language over the disjoint union of $\alpha$ and the bits $\{\mathbf{t}, \mathbf{f}\}$ consisting of the words in which every symbol is a bit, including the empty word.
nodes.title: Words of bits

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the language over the disjoint union of $\alpha$ and the bits $\{\mathbf{t}, \mathbf{f}\}$ consisting of the bit words $c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$ with $n \ge 0$ and $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$, where $c(j) = \mathbf{t}\,\mathbf{f}^j$ is the unary code of $j$. In particular it contains the empty word.
nodes.title: Codes of index sequences below $k$

nodes.summary: Let $w$ and $x$ be words over an alphabet $\alpha$ such that $w$ is not a prefix of $x$. Then there is a position $m < |w|$ with the following property: writing $w = u\,c\,r$ with $|u| = m$ and $c \in \alpha$, either $x = u$, or $x = u\,a\,y$ for some letter $a \ne c$ and some word $y$.
nodes.title: A word that does not start with $w$ leaves $w$ at some position

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types, call the elements of $\alpha$ letters and those of $\beta$ bits, and regard words over $\alpha$ and over $\beta$ as words over the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$. If $u\,b\,z = X\,Y$ for words $u, z$ over $\alpha \oplus \beta$, a bit $b$, a word $X$ of letters and a word $Y$ of bits, then there are words $Y_1, Y_2$ of bits with $Y = Y_1 Y_2$ and $b\,z = Y_2$.
nodes.title: A bit inside a word of letters followed by bits starts a suffix of the bits

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$. The universality grammar of $P$ generates every word over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ if and only if the Post correspondence problem $P$ has no solution.
nodes.title: The universality grammar generates every word exactly when PCP has no solution

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$. The assignment of intended languages to the nonterminals of the universality grammar of $P$ is a valuation of that grammar: for every production $A \to \gamma$, the language that $\gamma$ denotes under the assignment is contained in the language assigned to $A$.
nodes.title: The intended languages form a valuation of the universality grammar

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $P$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$ of length $m$, and for $i < m$ let $t_i$ and $b_i$ be the top and bottom words of the domino of $P$ at position $i$, counting from $0$. Read the bit $\mathrm{true}$ as the separator $|$ and the bit $\mathrm{false}$ as $1$, and let $c(i)$ be the unary code of $i$: the bit $|$ followed by $i$ bits $1$. The language…
nodes.title: The language of the universality grammar

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language of words of letters is the set of all words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ whose symbols all lie in $\alpha$, that is, the words over $\alpha$ (including the empty word) viewed as words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.
nodes.title: Words of letters

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language of nonempty words of letters is the set of all nonempty words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ whose symbols all lie in $\alpha$, that is, the nonempty words over $\alpha$ viewed as words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$.
nodes.title: Nonempty words of letters

nodes.summary: Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$, let $s$ be a function sending each domino to a word over $\alpha$ (for instance its top word), and write $w_i = s(d_i)$. The list language of $s$ and $P$ is the language over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ of all words $w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$ with $n \ge 1$ and $i_1, \dots, i_n < m$, where $c(i)$ is the unary code of $i$:…
nodes.title: List language of a PCP instance

nodes.summary: Let $P = (d_0, \dots, d_{m-1})$ be a list of dominoes over $\alpha$, let $s$ be a function sending each domino to a word over $\alpha$, and set $w_i = s(d_i)$ for $i < m$ and $w_i = s(\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ for $i \ge m$, where $(\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ is the domino with empty top and bottom. The list word of an index sequence $i_1, \dots, i_n$ is the word $w_{i_1} \cdots w_{i_n}\, c(i_n) \cdots c(i_1)$…
nodes.title: List word of an index sequence

nodes.summary: Consider words over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, whose symbols are letters from $\alpha$ and bits, and read the bit $\mathrm{true}$ as the separator $|$ and the bit $\mathrm{false}$ as $1$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a word is malformed with bound $k$ when at least one of the following holds: it consists of letters only (possibly none); it is a word of letters followed by a nonempty word of bits whose first bit is…
nodes.title: Malformed words

nodes.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $w$ be a word over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$. Then $w$ is malformed with bound $k$, or $w = x\, c(j_1) \cdots c(j_n)$ for a word $x$ over $\alpha$ and a nonempty sequence of indices $j_1, \dots, j_n < k$, where $c(j)$ is the unary code of $j$: the bit $\mathrm{true}$ followed by $j$ bits $\mathrm{false}$.
nodes.title: Every word is malformed or well formed

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding. There is a computable map sending each PCP instance $P$ (a list of dominoes over $\alpha$) to an encoded context-free grammar $G_P$ over the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ (the letters of $\alpha$ together with two bits) such that $P$ has no PCP solution if and only if $G_P$ generates every word over…
nodes.title: The complement of PCP many-one reduces to universality of context-free grammars

nodes.summary: Let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each nonterminal. For terminal words $u$ and $v$, a nonterminal $A$ and a word $w$, the word $w$ lies in the language that $V$ assigns to the sentential form $u\,A\,v$ if and only if $w = u z v$ for some $z \in V(A)$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a form with one nonterminal

nodes.summary: Let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each nonterminal. For terminal words $u$, $v$ and $x$, nonterminals $A$ and $B$ and a word $w$, the word $w$ lies in the language that $V$ assigns to the sentential form $u\,A\,v\,B\,x$ if and only if $w = u z_1 v z_2 x$ for some $z_1 \in V(A)$ and $z_2 \in V(B)$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a form with two nonterminals

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes over a finite alphabet with decidable equality, $A$ a nonterminal, $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom), $i < |P|$ an index, $w = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$, and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ the unary code of $i$ as bits. Write letters and bits as terminals and $N_3$, $N_4$, $N_7$ for the nonterminals $3$, $4$ and $7$. Each of the following encoded…
nodes.title: Membership in the mismatch productions

nodes.summary: The mismatch language of one side of a list $P$ of dominoes. Let $s$ be a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom), write $w_i = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$ and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ for the unary code of $i$ as bits. The language, over letters and bits, consists of the words $x\,\mathrm{code}(i_n) \cdots \mathrm{code}(i_1)$ where $x$ is a word of letters and $i_1, \dots, i_n$ with…
nodes.title: The mismatch language

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes over a finite alphabet, $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom), $w_i = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$, and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ the unary code of $i$ as bits. Let $A$ be a nonterminal such that every mismatch production of $A$ for $s$ and $P$ is a production of the universality grammar of $P$. Then for every nonempty sequence $i_1, \dots, i_n$ of…
nodes.title: Every mismatched word is derivable from the mismatch nonterminal

nodes.summary: The mismatch productions of a nonterminal $A$ for one side of a list $P$ of dominoes over a finite alphabet. Let $s$ be a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). For each index $i < |P|$ write $w = s(d_i)$ for the $i$-th domino $d_i$ of $P$ and $\mathrm{code}(i)$ for the unary code of $i$ as bits. With letters and bits as terminals and $N_3$, $N_4$, $N_7$ the nonterminals $3$, $4$, $7$ (meant to…
nodes.title: The mismatch productions

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes and $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). Write the code of an index $i$ as the bits $|\,1^i$, where $|$ stands for the bit true and $1$ for the bit false. A word over letters and bits that is malformed with respect to $|P|$ (it has no bits, its first bit is a $1$, a bit is followed by a letter, or it contains the factor $|\,1^{|P|}$) does not belong to the…
nodes.title: Malformed words are in no list language

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a list of dominoes and $s$ a map from dominoes to words (in use, the top or the bottom). No word of the mismatch language of $s$ for $P$ belongs to the list language of $s$ for $P$.
nodes.title: Mismatched words are not in the list language

nodes.summary: For a letter $a$ of a finite alphabet with decidable equality, the list of all letters $b$ of the alphabet with $b \ne a$, in the order of a fixed enumeration of the alphabet.
nodes.title: The letters other than a given letter

nodes.summary: A list $P$ of dominoes has a PCP solution if and only if some word belongs both to the list language of the top words of $P$ and to the list language of the bottom words of $P$.
nodes.title: A PCP instance is solvable exactly when its top and bottom list languages meet

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a bit $b$, the terminal $b$ of the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar, that is, the element $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inr}\, b)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.
nodes.title: Encoded bit terminal

nodes.summary: For a letter $a \in \alpha$, the terminal $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar, that is, the element $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{inl}\, a)$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.
nodes.title: Encoded letter terminal

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a natural number $A$, the nonterminal $A$ as a symbol of an encoded grammar over the alphabet $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$, that is, the element $\mathrm{inl}\, A$ of $\mathbb{N} \oplus (\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool})$.
nodes.title: Encoded nonterminal

nodes.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the encoded context-free grammar over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ with start nonterminal $0$ whose productions are the base productions for $k = |P|$, followed by the mismatch productions of the top words of $P$ with nonterminal $1$, followed by the mismatch productions of the bottom words of $P$ with nonterminal $2$.
nodes.title: The universality grammar

nodes.summary: For a list $P$ of dominoes over $\alpha$, the assignment of a language over $\alpha \oplus \mathrm{Bool}$ to each natural number that sends $0$ to the union of the malformed language for $k = |P|$ and the mismatch languages of the top words and of the bottom words of $P$; $1$ to the mismatch language of the top words of $P$; $2$ to the mismatch language of the bottom words of $P$; $3$ to the words of letters; $4$…
nodes.title: Intended languages of the nonterminals of the universality grammar
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
